This is interesting because I'm not religious but I find almost as interesting as '1984' or 'Animal Farm'. Because instead of devil I would substitute politician.

The problem that we're facing is the same thing that Paul Harvey was discussing in 1965. He was a radio host, and discussed it in terms that his conservative audience would have understood quite well at the time. We're able to more clearly identify it now; that control breeds lust for more control. For many centuries, religion was the dominant form of control in the western world, but it also came with a code of respect and morality. Around the industrial revolution, religion was finally displaced as the dominant form of control. It was replaced by economics, and that ushered in a whole new set of people and policies at the top. Notice that I have not invoked the idea of government. Government was always and continues to be the subservient tool of a higher power. Now, the bright spot in the western world before the industrial revolution was the United States of America. Those who started America managed to shed themselves of the controlling aspects of organized religion, but they held onto their practices and morals and continued to be decent people. The country prospered, blah, blah, blah. But like the rest of the world, religion suffered defeat when the industrial revolution brought economics. Morality suffered too, and now we live in a world where people are ready and willing to do walk all over other people to get a bigger paycheck.

If people can learn morality in absence of religion, if people can learn to be aware of how they affect the world, that might be the key to breaking through our current difficulties. If not, we may be doomed to lose the progress of centuries before us.

Religion certainly had it's positive aspects in the past. Commandments and restrictions were around keeping families and communities together and productive. The bible warned against getting drugged out, had parables about civility and hospitality, told tales of the wicked getting punished. But also negative ones that demanded tribute, loyalty to kings and popes, among others.

The abandonment of religion should have been a huge advance for reason and liberty but instead ushered in an era of nihilistic hedonism. The baby was tossed with the bathwater.
